authority: Copyright Office, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

description.en: Copyright registration in India is administered by the Copyright Office under the Copyright Act, 1957. While copyright exists automatically upon creation of a work, registration provides prima facie evidence of ownership and is essential for enforcing rights in court. Registration covers literary, dramatic, musical, artistic works, cinematograph films, and sound recordings.

verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant must be the author of the work, the owner of copyright (through assignment or operation of law), or an authorized agent of the author/owner. In case of works created during employment, the employer is the first owner unless otherwise agreed.
The work must be original and must fall within the categories of works protectable under the Copyright Act: literary, dramatic, musical, artistic works, cinematograph films, or sound recordings.

unverifiedEligibility: Ideas, procedures, methods of operation, and mathematical concepts are not copyrightable — only the expression of ideas is protected.
Government works (Acts, rules, judicial decisions) are not eligible for copyright.
The work must not infringe on existing copyrights.
Foreign nationals can register if their country is a member of the Berne Convention or Universal Copyright Convention.

requirements.claim: Application in Form XIV (for literary, dramatic, musical, artistic works) or Form XIV with appropriate diary number. The application must contain complete particulars of the work and the applicant.
Three copies of the work being registered. For literary works, printed copies; for artistic works, photographs or reproductions; for software, source code printout and CD/DVD.
No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the author if the applicant is not the author. If the work is published, NOC from the publisher is also required.
Identity proof of the applicant (Aadhaar, PAN, passport, or voter ID). For companies, Certificate of Incorporation and authorization letter.
Power of Attorney (Vakalatnama) if the application is filed through an advocate or a registered copyright society.
A search report or declaration that no identical or similar work has been previously registered with the Copyright Office.

processInformation.claim: File the application online through the Copyright Office e-filing portal (copyright.gov.in) along with copies of the work and required documents. A diary number is issued upon filing.

After filing, there is a mandatory 30-day waiting period during which any person may file objections to the registration. The Copyright Office issues notice to the parties mentioned in the application.
If no objections are received or objections are resolved, the Registrar of Copyrights examines the application. A scrutiny letter (discrepancy letter) may be issued if corrections are needed.
Upon successful examination, the work is entered in the Register of Copyrights and a Registration Certificate is issued. The registration details are available in the public Copyright Register.

output.claim: A Copyright Registration Certificate is issued containing the registration number, title of work, class of work, name of author, name of copyright owner, and date of registration. The registration is valid for the lifetime of the author plus 60 years (literary, dramatic, musical, artistic works) or 60 years from publication (cinematograph films, sound recordings).

fees.applicability: Registration fee per literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work
fees.claim: The prescribed fee for registration of each literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work is Rs. 500.

fees.applicability: Registration fee per cinematograph film or sound recording
fees.claim: The prescribed fee for registration of each cinematograph film or sound recording is Rs. 2,000.

processingTime.applicability: Copyright registration from application to certificate
processingTime.claim: Copyright registration typically takes 30-60 days from the date of filing. The mandatory 30-day objection period constitutes the minimum processing time. Actual time may extend if discrepancy letters are issued or objections are filed.

sources.title: Copyright Office India — Official Portal
sources.publisher: Copyright Office, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Copyright Office portal provides online filing facility, application forms, fee schedule, search facility for registered works, and FAQs on copyright registration procedures in India.
claimsSupported: Applications can be filed online through the portal.
Fee is Rs. 500 for literary/artistic works and Rs. 2,000 for cinematograph/sound recordings.
Copies of the work and identity proof are required.
sources.uncertainty: Fee schedules and procedural requirements may be updated through official notifications.

sources.title: The Copyright Act, 1957 and Copyright Rules, 2013
sources.publisher: Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Copyright Act, 1957 (as amended by the Copyright Amendment Act, 2012) governs copyright protection in India. Chapter X of the Act deals with registration of copyright. The Copyright Rules, 2013 prescribe the forms, fees, and procedures for registration.
claimsSupported: Copyright protection is automatic upon creation; registration provides legal evidence.
Duration is author's lifetime plus 60 years for literary/artistic works.
Duration is 60 years from publication for films and sound recordings.
30-day objection period after filing is mandatory.
sources.uncertainty: The Act may be amended. Judicial interpretations continue to evolve copyright scope.

limitations: This record covers the general copyright registration process. Specific procedures may vary by type of work.
The record does not cover copyright assignment, licensing, or enforcement procedures.
International copyright protection (through Berne Convention) is not detailed.
Software copyright registration may have additional requirements not fully captured here.
The record does not cover related rights (performers' rights, broadcast reproduction rights).
Fee amounts are subject to periodic revision.
